The dispute is not error-transport hygiene but whether these values are legal input at all — the documentation publishes no charset constraint while the runtime enforces one.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: index deletion (existing or not) returns HTTP 200; missing collection returns 404
contract_grounding.note: api_violates_assertion=true chosen honestly per the self-check: the observed dispositions (HTTP 400) for plain-string field_name values on a live collection with no index are outside the asserted 200-promise and outside any documented charset restriction — field_name is documented (page + OpenAPI ytt + JsonPath's own JsonSchema impl) as unconstrained string, so at the doc face these inputs are legal and the 400 contradicts the quote. The competing reading — that the promise's domain presumes grammar-valid names per the source's JsonPath grammar (unquoted keys limited to alphanumeric/_/-, quoting escape hatch exists so '"f kw"' with literal double quotes would parse) — is a source-level mitigation the doc never states; it cannot flip the doc-face violation and is left to the auditor.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST: #[delete("/collections/{collection_name}/index/{field_name}")] (update_api.rs:410) -> actix Path<FieldPath> extraction -> FieldPath.name: JsonPath (update_api.rs:27-30) -> JsonPath::deserialize (json_path/mod.rs:516) -> FromStr -> parse::json_path nom grammar (parse.rs:28-40) where raw_str accepts only is_alphanumeric()||'_'||'-' (parse.rs:42-47) -> failure mapped to serde custom error 'Invalid json path: <value>' -> actix renders HTTP 400 'Deserialize error in path parameters: ...'. gRPC: update_common.rs:719/761/794/825 field_name = json_path_from_proto(...) (conversions/json.rs:44) -> same grammar -> Status::invalid_argument. Meanwhile the published contract surfaces no constraint: JsonPath's JsonSchema impl returns String::json_schema (mod.rs:525-537) and openapi-collections.ytt.yaml:207-212 declares field_name type: string with no pattern — so ' ', 'f kw', '中文🎯' (emoji char not alphanumeric; CJK chars alone would pass), decoded '..' all fail the UNDOCUMENTED grammar and are rejected 400, while grammar-valid names ('a'*1024, dotted nested paths, double-quoted keys like "f kw") parse and proceed to the idempotent-delete logic which returns 200 for non-existent indexes.
